objective: Improve robust per-map anomaly detection without fitting to the public test data.
official_performance: Unknown. No R1 or R2 leaderboard score has been reported in this session; no automatic submission was made.

research_basis.finding: The organizer's paper compares physical power-spectrum, CNN and autoencoder baselines; parameter-inference success does not ensure strong OOD detection.
research_basis.decision: Keep physical summaries and a nearest-cluster control. Preserve the official shape-noise, mask, nuisance distributions and low-FPR metric. Do not compare our synthetic probe scores numerically with the paper's official scores.

research_basis.finding: The authors found field-level continuous-time flow density models more effective than compressed scattering/CNN feature models for their weak-lensing mismatch examples, under simplified forward models and noise settings.
research_basis.decision: Implement a separate masked JAX field-flow pilot and check its ODE/Jacobian numerics before treating it as an anomaly detector. Our 2x2-pooled, small-UNet implementation is inspired by the paper, not a faithful reproduction.

research_basis.finding: Scattering summaries can retain non-Gaussian cosmological information with fixed, interpretable filters.
research_basis.decision: Test custom masked Morlet summaries as complementary features. Distinguish this implementation from standard Kymatio scattering. Adding all 144 coefficients degraded our early probes; 16 train-fitted principal components largely restored performance without a clear gain.

research_basis.finding: Generative ensembles and likelihood disagreement can help detect failures of individual density models.
research_basis.decision: Compare three initialization seeds, averaged latent energy, average likelihood and a WAIC-style mean-NLL plus variance score. Here, average latent energy performed better on the engineered probes; WAIC did not dominate. Initialization seeds are not posterior draws.

research_basis.finding: Background statistics can confound likelihood-based OOD detection; likelihood-ratio controls can reduce those effects.
research_basis.decision: Test conditional shape models given the 20 observed power-spectrum summaries. They trade sensitivity across shift families and should not automatically replace a joint model.

research_basis.finding: Scale-dependent summaries and evidence can expose simulation mismatch; a shift may bias parameters without looking unusual in a limited representation.
research_basis.decision: Audit multiple spatial scales and retain diverse diagnostics instead of optimizing a single reconstruction metric.

research_basis.finding: Ding et al. report that diffusion likelihood in learned representation space can avoid some failures of pixel-space likelihood on their image benchmarks.
research_basis.decision: Representation and score choice deserve separate ablations. Their pretrained natural-image encoders and image OOD benchmarks do not establish effectiveness on masked cosmological fields.

research_basis.finding: Jarve et al. evaluate diffusion density on pretrained encoder representations; likelihood optimality requires assumptions about the alternative distribution.
research_basis.decision: Do not assume fitting the normal distribution alone determines the best detector for unknown physical alternatives.

research_basis.finding: Kamkari et al. pair likelihood with local intrinsic dimensionality to distinguish density from probability mass in generative OOD detection.
research_basis.decision: Check two-sided and geometric diagnostics; do not treat high likelihood as sufficient evidence that a map is physically normal. LID itself has not been implemented here.

research_basis.finding: Armijo et al. report that weak-lensing flows can recover marginal moments while misestimating cross-statistic covariances, and examine noise/data augmentation as mitigations.
research_basis.decision: Audit the Gaussianized latent covariance on normal validation data. Test a separately fitted shrinkage covariance using normal-only CV before increasing model size.

research_basis.finding: Armijo et al. combine power spectra and Minkowski functionals in HSC-Y1 cosmological inference; the morphology summaries add non-Gaussian information.
research_basis.decision: A targeted next representation is multiscale area, boundary length and Euler characteristic, with fixed survey-mask handling. This is a proposed anomaly-detection experiment, not evidence of OOD improvement from that paper.

protocol.splits: Per cosmology: 160 fitting, 32 normal validation, 32 calibration, 32 audit realizations; fixed seed 2026.
protocol.audit_status: The audit set and R1 synthetic families have now been reused during development. They are not a pristine final holdout.
protocol.selection: Normal validation selects density checkpoints. Engineered probes inform the choice of score and representation. Equal-weight ensemble averaging is fixed before public-test inference.
protocol.uncertainty: Paired bootstraps resample the same positives and calibration maps for both methods, preserving normal cosmology proportions. They quantify conditional sampling uncertainty, not unknown OOD physics or selection bias.
protocol.new_morphology_probe: Masked IAAFT on 256 reused normal audit maps preserves the valid-pixel histogram exactly, but leaves a median relative Fourier-amplitude error of 0.1067. It is not a pure higher-order-only intervention.
protocol.public_test: Only frozen, pointwise inference on the current v2 file; no public-test calibration, normalization, adaptation, pooled ranks or model selection.

completed_main_comparison.meaning: Mean TPR across the competition's 100 log-spaced FPRs, evaluated on engineered synthetic probes. These are not official competition scores.
completed_main_comparison.normal_audit: At the calibration 1% threshold: R1 distance flagged 32/3232 normal audit maps, worst cosmology 8/32; the flow ensemble flagged 34/3232, worst cosmology 2/32. Small group counts and repeated audit use limit interpretation.

candidate.checks: Singleton, reversed-batch and split-batch predictions were identical for fixed verification maps.

open_questions: Do candidates 04 and 05 improve official performance? No official scores have been reported.
Would averaging trace probes improve final-score stability enough to justify extra inference cost? The measured normal-data median score change across probes was 0.0514.
Does normal-only covariance calibration improve flow goodness of fit without erasing genuine anomaly directions?
Would fresh-noise feature augmentation improve covariance and low-FPR tails? Independent noise views do not add independent simulator realizations.
How robust are choices made on reused synthetic families to genuinely new physical misspecification?
Can a new learned representation retain non-Gaussian morphology while ignoring permitted nuisance variation?

field_study.models: Two independent masked field flow-matching models, seeds 0 and 1; each 4000 updates on fresh shape noise, 2x2 pooled inputs, width-16 UNet, EMA checkpoints.
field_study.paper_scope: The Diao et al. field model was trained unconditionally across cosmologies. Its main OOD comparison fixed test cosmology; its compressed-feature models had idealized true-cosmology conditioning. It is not the same nuisance-marginalized experiment as ours.
field_study.numerics: 32-step Heun integration; one fixed Rademacher trace probe (seed 451). On 32 normal maps, seed-0 median NLL difference from 64 steps was 0.684 versus normal NLL std about 864. Additional trace-seed audit is running. Completed four-probe audit on 128 normal calibration maps: median single-probe NLL SD about 16; two-seed ensemble median 15.65 versus conditional normal SD 115.98. Holding regressors fixed, changing the probe caused median absolute final-score difference 0.0514 and 95th percentile 0.1691.
field_study.discovery: Raw field likelihood was a poor anomaly score. A normal-only ridge fit to 20 log powers and their exponentials predicts about 98 percent of its normal variance in grouped cross-validation. The absolute, heteroskedastic residual is much better on peak shifts. This is a residual score, not an exact likelihood ratio.
field_study.regression_fit: 512 normal validation maps. Five-fold CV grouped by cosmology chooses ridge strength and input basis; calibration/audit maps do not fit the regressors. Development positives reuse the 512 fitting maps.
field_study.ensemble: Candidate 05 averages candidate 04 and the corrected two-model field score, each scaled using normal-calibration median and q90-minus-median; weights 1/2,1/2.

comparison.limitations: Sampling intervals condition on the fitted models, observed cosmologies and chosen artificial shifts. They exclude selection bias and unknown OOD physics.

field_study.status: Candidate 05 exported, full TPU API and packaged CLI passed exact equivalence on eight fixed reference inputs; 10000 finite scores; not submitted.

trace_audit.interpretation: Changing the fixed probe while holding the normal-trained regression/calibration fixed. Not an official score uncertainty interval; no public data used.

submission_strategy: Prefer the two complementary R2 hypotheses (04 and 05 once verified) over spending all five daily slots on minor variants. Do not average or tune using pooled public-test inputs. Daily/account remaining quota is not known here; no automatic uploads were made.

next_experiments.test: Fresh shape-noise views for the physical-summary flows, keeping simulator-realization splits fixed.
next_experiments.reason: The current summary flows use one cached noise view per training realization. Noise augmentation could improve density estimation; it does not increase independent cosmological simulations.

next_experiments.test: Small multiscale morphology and regional-summary descriptors with a regularized conditional flow.
next_experiments.reason: Targets morphology and spatial-modulation weaknesses. Fixed-mask topology and regional statistics may complement pooled global summaries; this is not yet implemented.

next_experiments.test: Average several fixed trace probes, then refit normal-only field residual regressors before evaluating new proxies.
next_experiments.reason: Probe noise is small relative to raw NLL but material after subtraction of its expected power dependence.

next_experiments.test: Noise-view self-supervision with an anti-collapse objective and separate physical-parameter heads.
next_experiments.reason: The R1 reconstruction/parameter models did not dominate physical summaries; representation diversity needs a different objective, not just another global autoencoder size.

additional_family_interpretation: The frozen hybrid improves stronger blending from 0.0425 to 0.1004 and strong spectral/peak shifts, but both models remain weak on spatial modulation (0.0462 versus 0.0393 at strength 0.5). It is not a universally stronger detector.
